## Deck Goal
Teach frontend-oriented AEM developers to introduce one reusable OSGi capability, configure it safely for AEM as a Cloud Service and choose the smallest delivery surface that serves a real consumer.

## Required Background
{
  "deck_context": {
    "source_summary": "Class 18 follows the Sling Models and Model Exporter lesson. It teaches when reusable work belongs in an OSGi service, how Declarative Services owns lifecycle and dependencies, how typed configuration becomes effective in AEM as a Cloud Service, and why a new servlet is justified only by a distinct HTTP consumer and contract.",
    "core_claim": "Add only the boundary the consumer needs: one reusable service capability, one safe effective configuration and no new servlet unless an existing rendering or export surface cannot satisfy a real HTTP contract.",
    "canonical_facts": [
      "A service should own one reusable capability needed by at least one real consumer.",
      "Declarative Services registers components, manages their lifecycle and resolves declared service references.",
      "A required unsatisfied service reference prevents component activation.",
      "OSGi Metatype annotations describe typed operator-facing configuration metadata.",
      "@Designate connects a Declarative Services component PID to an Object Class Definition.",
      "AEM as a Cloud Service supports author or publish plus dev, stage or prod run modes; custom run modes are not supported.",
      "For one PID, the configuration with the most matching run modes is effective as a whole; properties are not merged from less-specific files.",
      "$[env:NAME] represents a non-secret environment-specific value and $[secret:NAME] represents a secret value.",
      "Environment variables must not override Adobe-owned OSGi configuration.",
      "Local runtime state is inspected in the SDK Web Console; cloud state is inspected in Developer Console status dumps.",
      "HTL, a Sling Model, a Core Component or an existing Model Exporter contract should be preferred before a new servlet.",
      "Sling strongly recommends resource-type servlet registration over path binding.",
      "A servlet registration should constrain methods, selectors and extensions to the real contract.",
      "A new endpoint adds validation, authorization, caching and compatibility responsibilities."
    ],
    "canonical_terms": [
      "OSGi service",
      "Declarative Services",
      "@Component",
      "@Reference",
      "@ObjectClassDefinition",
      "@AttributeDefinition",
      "@Designate",
      "PID",
      "author",
      "publish",
      "dev",
      "stage",
      "prod",
      "$[env:GUIDE_BASE_URL]",
      "$[secret:GUIDE_API_TOKEN]",
      "Web Console",
      "Developer Console",
      "HTL",
      "Sling Model",
      "Model Exporter",
      "resource type",
      "selector",
      "extension",
      "method"
    ]
  },
  "slide_local_context": {
    "required_background": "Place GUIDE URL CONFIG in the center with exact annotations @ObjectClassDefinition and @AttributeDefinition. Show two typed methods: String base_url() and boolean enabled() default true. Flow to GENERATED METATYPE METADATA, then @Designate(ocd = GuideUrlConfig.class), then the service PID, then ACTIVATE WITH TYPED CONFIG. Add OPERATIONAL API as the conclusion."
  }
}
